messages.subject: Advice on logistic regression
parts:
Does anyone have a recommendation on what package should be used for a
simple logistic regression?

messages.author: 963b6d84a823404f
messages.subject: Re: Advice on logistic regression
parts:
It's built in. Use glm() with family=binomial(link=logit).

See Venables & Ripley, Modern Applied Statistics with S, 4th edition,
Sec 7.2 (pg 190).

karl

messages.author: c91a208fffacfb7e
messages.subject: Re: Advice on logistic regression
parts: On Tue, Sep 15, 2009 at 2:48 PM, Karl Broman <kbr...@biostat.wisc.edu> wrote:
> It's built in.  Use glm() with family=binomial(link=logit).

Well, technically it is in the stats package, which is attached by
default. The perverse user could force R to start without the stats
package and therefore would not have the glm function available.

(There can be non-perverse reasons for eliminating packages that are
attached by default. If you are using R as a scripting language and
starting it with Rscript or r (from the "littler" package) then you
might want to strip it down to the most basic packages so that it
starts faster.)
